page_title: How to create HTTP Server in Java - ServerSocket Example

sources.entry: Build a Simple HTTP Server with Java

summary.title: How to create HTTP Server in Java - ServerSocket Example
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a minimal single-threaded HTTP server in Java using ServerSocket and Socket, reading the browser's request and sending back a plain response.
keywords: build web server from scratch java
single client at a time server
takeaways: Create a ServerSocket on port 8080 and call accept() in a loop to receive client connections.
Read the HTTP request line and headers from the client socket's input stream with a BufferedReader.
Write an HTTP/1.1 200 OK status line, blank line, and body to the socket's output stream.
Use try-with-resources (Java 7) so the client socket closes automatically after each response.
The server handles only one client at a time, which is a limitation of this simple design.
summary.summary: The article walks through building a basic HTTP server in Java step by step. It starts with a ServerSocket listening on port 8080, then adds a blocking accept() loop, reads the raw GET request sent by a browser, and finally writes a simple HTTP 200 response containing today's date. Testing is done by connecting from a browser and using telnet. The author notes the design serves one client at a time.
